newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Renault workers take protest into France.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Renault workers take protest into France.

text.p: About 1,000 workers at Renault SA's Belgian factory crossed into northern France Wednesday to seek support from French colleagues in their campaign against the automaker's decision to shut down the plant.
The Belgian workers from the Vilvoorde plant cut through wire mesh to enter a Renault plant at Douai and discuss the controversial closure scheduled to take place in July.
Renault France said last Thursday, unexpectedly and without consulting the workforce, that it would close its assembly plant at Vilvoorde near Brussels with the loss of 3,100 jobs.
Renault Paris defended its decision as necessary for the survival of the group.
Chanting "Renault, Belgium, Open" and "Douai, Vilvoorde Solidarity," the Belgian protesters toured workshops at the Douai plant and handed out leaflets.
They met more sympathy that solidarity from their French colleagues who worry about their own jobs.
"We'll express solidarity but one has to admit that individualism is the rule," said Jean-Pierre Garnier, a representative of the CFDT trade union at the Douai plant.
"Workers fear for their jobs and wages. Organising a protest against that background is difficult," he said.
Managagement is preparing to cut 167 of the 6,000 jobs at the Douai plant by encouraging early retirement and part-time work.
